instruction: more_itertools.split_before, split_after and split_when disagree with themselves on an empty iterable: with maxsplit=0 they yield one empty list ([[]]), while with any other maxsplit (including the default -1) they yield nothing ([]). Make maxsplit=0 also yield nothing for an empty iterable in these three functions; a non-empty iterable with maxsplit=0 still gives a single list holding all of it. split_at is not affected and must keep following str.split: for an empty iterable it yields one empty list for every maxsplit, as ''.split(',', 0) == [''].
